channel.title: Keryx
channel.description: Aleksa and Juno discuss AI and tech news, daily. Each morning, Aleksa and Juno break down the day's biggest stories — data centers, chips, frontier models, AI agents, and the companies building them — with jokes, hot takes, and plain English: what actually happened, why it matters, and what the headline numbers leave out. A fast, funny briefing for people building with AI, or just trying to keep up with it. New episodes every morning. Free show.
channel.itunes:author: Aleksa & Juno

item.title: Keryx - November 12, 2026: Signal's Proof, Gemini Decides, TSMC's Forty Billion
item.description: DeepMind proves the actual Signal binary keeps messages secret, Google's Decisions API scores a thousand options without writing a word, and TSMC authorizes forty-one billion dollars for fabs and packaging. Plus the Nvidia board crisis around Jensen Huang and Anthropic's trillion-dollar IPO roadshow.

item.title: Keryx - November 11, 2026: Fable's Cheaper Tokens, Nvidia Prunes, OpenAI's Kill Switch
item.description: Anthropic cuts Fable's token prices by twenty percent while Nvidia prunes a giant model to fit a single serving GPU, and OpenAI builds a kill switch with a thirty-five second stop clock. Plus Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, Liquid AI's tiny edge model, and GitHub's Copilot runtime rewrite in Rust.

item.title: Keryx - November 10, 2026: Quantum Proof, LinkedIn's Second Opinion, Uber's Agent Guardrails
item.description: A machine-checked proof narrows where quantum speedups can hide, LinkedIn lets a second model double-check a lone reviewer's finding, and Uber traces every privileged agent action back to the user's actual request. Plus Google's new TPU systems and Anthropic's take on agent memory.

item.title: Keryx - November 9, 2026: Engineering Agents Miss the Sign-Off
item.description: Claude Opus 5.5 leads a brutal engineering exam but only 41 percent of its designs clear every hard check, GPT-6 Astra writes working game weights, and Anthropic's FlashProve makes model substitution auditable. Plus Marvell's 115 billion dollar optics bet and the real story behind Anthropic's generator orders.

item.title: Keryx - November 8, 2026
item.description: Data-center politics, China's 800 volt live deployment, Microsoft's Oracle exit, and the latest from X.
